answer: Temporal footprint reconciliation. Each agent identity must carry a continuously renewed history of low-value interactions with distinct counterparties; new accounts start at zero depth. An attacker cloning identities pays the full interaction cost per clone, with no bulk discount. Diminishing returns mean the tenth clone costs more than the first, mirroring how timber rings accrue slowly. The system tolerates a thin echo of duplicate accounts rather than banning them. Forging depth at ocean scale becomes prohibitively expensive.
